Regarding what we were discussing in previous sessions concerning the explanation of the noble verses: we had reached Surah al-Mutaffifin, so let us speak briefly on what is within reach of it. We say: Allah began this surah with the word ﴿Woe﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 1], and "Woe" (wayl) is repeated many times in the Qur'an. It is, according to the most correct view, a word of warning (wa'id) by which Allah, glory be to Him, threatens whoever opposes His command or commits His prohibition, in the manner specified in the sentence that follows it.

Here the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Woe to those who give less [than due]﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 1]. So who are these al-Mutaffifun (those who give less than due)?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 83, verses 2–3:

These defrauders (al-mutaffifun) are explained by the verses that follow, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Those who, when they take a measure from people, take it in full, but when they measure or weigh for them, they cause loss.﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 2, 3].

﴿When they take a measure from people﴾ means: when they buy from them what is measured, they take from them the right in full, without any shortfall.

﴿But when they measure or weigh for them﴾ means: when they measure for others, such as when they are the ones who sell food by measure, or when they sell something to people by weight, they cause a shortfall when they measure or weigh for people; ﴿they cause loss﴾. These people, may Allah protect us, take their own right in full and diminish the right of others. Thus they combine two things: stinginess (shuhh) and miserliness (bukhl). Shuhh is in seeking their right in full without consideration or leniency, and bukhl is in withholding what is obligatory upon them, namely completing the measure and the weight.

This example that Allah the Mighty and Majestic mentioned concerning measure and weight is in reality an example, so everything resembling it is measured against it. Everyone who demands his right in full from the one who owes it, while withholding the right that he himself owes, is included in this noble verse. For instance, a husband wants his wife to give him his right in full and does not slacken in any part of his right, yet when it comes to fulfilling her right, he is lax and does not give her what is hers. How often do women complain of this type of husband, may Allah protect us. Many husbands want their wives to fulfill their rights in full, yet they themselves do not give their wives their rights in full; perhaps they diminish most of her right to maintenance, kind companionship and other things.

Strange, brothers, is that this occurs among many people who appear to be committed, to the point that some women say: "I only chose to accept this husband because of his good reputation and commitment." Then he turns out to be in a worse state toward his wife than the people of sinfulness. I do not know about these people who appear committed: do they think that commitment means a person worships Allah alone and wastes the rights of people?! Wronging people is more severe than a person wronging himself in regard to the right of Allah, because a person wronging himself in regard to the right of Allah is under the Will (of Allah) if it is short of shirk: if Allah wills, He forgives him, and if He wills, He punishes him for it. But the rights of the children of Adam are not under the Will; they must be paid. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whom do you count as bankrupt among you?" They said: "One who has no dirham or dinar." Or they said: "Nor goods." He said: "No, the bankrupt is one who comes on the Day of Resurrection with good deeds like mountains (many), then he comes having wronged this one, cursed this one, struck this one, and taken the wealth of this one. So this one takes from his good deeds, and this one from his good deeds, and this one from his good deeds, and this one from his good deeds. If some of his good deeds remain, (well); otherwise, some of their sins are taken and cast upon him, then he is cast into the Fire."[[Recorded by Muslim (2581/59) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah radiya Allahu 'anhu that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do you know who the bankrupt is?" They said: "The bankrupt among us is one who has no dirham or goods." He said: "Indeed, the bankrupt of my ummah is one who comes on the Day of Resurrection with prayer, fasting and zakat, but comes having cursed this one, slandered this one, consumed the wealth of this one, shed the blood of this one, and struck this one. So this one is given from his good deeds and this one from his good deeds. If his good deeds are exhausted before what is owed is settled, some of their sins are taken and cast upon him, then he is cast into the Fire."]]. So my advice to those brothers who neglect the rights of their wives, whether they are among the committed or others, is that they fear Allah the Exalted. The Prophet ﷺ enjoined this in the greatest gathering witnessed by the Islamic world during the lifetime of the Messenger ﷺ, on the Day of 'Arafah during the Farewell Pilgrimage. He said: "Fear Allah concerning women, for you have taken them under the trust of Allah, and you have made their private parts lawful by the word of Allah."[[Recorded by Muslim (1218/147) from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah.]] So we were commanded to fear Allah the Exalted concerning women. And he said: "Fear Allah concerning women, for they are 'awan (captives) with you."[[Recorded by Ahmad (20695) from the hadith of the paternal uncle of Abu Hurrah al-Raqashi radiya Allahu 'anhu, with the wording: "Indeed they are 'awan with you."]] That is, in the position of captives, because a captive, if his captor wills, releases him, and if he wills, keeps him. The woman with her husband is likewise: if he wills, he divorces her, and if he wills, he keeps her; she is in the position of a captive with him, so let him fear Allah concerning her.

Likewise we find some people who want their children to fulfill their rights completely, yet they themselves neglect the rights of their children. They want their children to honor them and fulfill their rights: to be dutiful to them with wealth, with their bodies, and in everything in which dutifulness is found, but he himself wastes these children, not fulfilling what is obligatory upon him toward them. We say: this man is a defrauder (mutaffif). As we say in the first matter, concerning the husband with his wife: if he wants her to fulfill his right in full while he diminishes her right, we say he is a defrauder. This father who wants his children to be dutiful to him in complete dutifulness while he falls short in their rights, we say to him: you are a defrauder. And we say to him: remember the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Woe to the defrauders, who, when they take a measure from people, take it in full, but when they measure or weigh for them, they cause loss.﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 1–3].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 83, verse 4–5:

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Do they not think that they will be resurrected, for a great Day?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 4, 5]. He means: Do these people not become certain and know with certainty? For the word "zann" (thinking, assuming) here carries the meaning of "yaqin" (certainty), and the use of "zann" in the sense of "yaqin" occurs frequently in the Qur'an, such as His saying: ﴿Those who think that they will meet their Lord and that they will return to Him﴾ [al-Baqarah 46]. So He says ﴿those who think that they will meet their Lord﴾ while they are certain that they will meet Allah. However, "zann" is frequently used in the sense of "yaqin" in the Arabic language.

Here the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Do they not think that they will be resurrected﴾, meaning: do these people not become certain that they will be resurrected; that is, brought out from their graves before the Lord of the worlds.

﴿For a great Day﴾. This Day is great, and there is no doubt that it is great, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a great thing﴾ [al-Hajj 1]; great in its length, in its terrors, in what happens in it, in every meaning that the word ﴿great﴾ carries.

But this great Day is difficult for some people and easy for others. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿For the disbelievers it is not easy﴾ [al-Muddaththir 10], and He said: ﴿The disbelievers say, "This is a difficult day"﴾ [al-Qamar 8]. But for the believers—may Allah make me and you among them—it is easy, as if they were performing an obligatory prayer, because of its ease for them and its lightness upon them, especially if one is among those who deserve this great protection and is among those whom Allah shades in His shade on a day when there is no shade but His shade. The point is that this is a great Day, but for people it is easy for some and difficult for others.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 83, verse 6:**

﴿On the Day when mankind stands before the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 6]. Meaning: this great Day is ﴿the Day when mankind stands before the Lord of the worlds﴾. They will rise from their graves barefoot, with neither sandals nor shoes, naked, with no clothing on them: no shirts, no trousers, no loincloths, and no cloaks. «Barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised»[[Reported by al-Bukhari (3349) and Muslim (2860/58), and the wording is Muslim's, with both their chains from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us giving a sermon and said: "O people, you will be gathered to Allah barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised. ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it; a promise upon Us. Indeed, We will do it﴾ [al-Anbiya': 104]..." The hadith continues.]] That is, uncircumcised. This means that the foreskin that is cut off in circumcision will return on the Day of Resurrection with its owner, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it﴾ [al-Anbiya': 104]. Allah, mighty and majestic, will restore it to demonstrate His complete power and that He recreates creation as He originated it. The foreskin was cut off in this world for the sake of cleanliness from filth, because if it remained, some urine would be trapped in it and it would be exposed to contamination. But in the Hereafter there is no need for this, because the Hereafter is not an abode of obligation (taklif) but an abode of recompense (jaza'). Yet Allah, glorified and exalted, may impose a test there, as He says: ﴿On the Day when the shin will be uncovered and they will be summoned to prostrate, but they will not be able [to do so]. Their eyes will be humbled; humiliation will cover them, and they had been summoned to prostration while they were sound﴾ [al-Qalam: 42-43]. The essential point is that people will stand in this condition: «barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised». In some hadiths the wording is: «buhman»[[Reported by Ahmad (16042) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Unays, may Allah be pleased with him, and the wording is: «People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, or he said: the servants, naked, uncircumcised, and buhman».]]. The scholars said: (al-buhm) means those who have no wealth with them. On the Day of Resurrection there is no wealth by which a person can ransom himself from punishment. On that Day no son will avail his father anything, nor will a father avail his son anything, nor a companion, nor a tribe. Each one says: "Myself, myself." ﴿For every person among them, that Day, there will be a matter that preoccupies him﴾ [Abasa: 37]. We ask Allah, the Exalted, to help us and you to bear its terrors and to make it easy for us.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿On the Day when mankind stands before the Lord of the worlds﴾, and He is Allah, majestic and exalted. On this Day all dominion will vanish except the dominion of the Lord of the worlds, majestic and exalted. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The Day they will come forth, nothing of them will be hidden from Allah. ﴾"To whom belongs dominion this Day?" ﴿It is to Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ (16). ﴿This Day every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. No injustice this Day. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ [Ghafir: 16-17].

Here our discussion of these noble verses of Surah al-Mutaffifin comes to an end.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 83, verse 7:

(...) In the commentary on Surat al-Mutaffifin, at which we have arrived at the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Nay! Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin. (7) And what will make you know what Sijjin is?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 7, 8] and so on to the end.

﴿Nay﴾ (kalla), when it occurs in the Qur'an, has meanings according to the context. It may be a particle of deterrence and rebuke, it may mean "truly," and it may have other meanings that the context determines, because words in the Arabic language do not have an intrinsic meaning that they cannot go beyond; rather, many Arabic words have meanings that vary according to the context of speech.

In this verse He says: ﴿Nay! Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin﴾. It may therefore mean: "Truly, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin." Or it may mean a deterrence from denying the Day of Recompense. In either case, Allah the Exalted makes clear in this noble verse that the record of the wicked is in Sijjin.

As for "Sijjin," the scholars said that it is derived from "sijn" (imprisonment), which means constriction, i.e., in a narrow place. This narrow place is the Fire of Hell, may Allah protect us, as Allah the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And when they are thrown into a narrow place of it, chained together, they will call out there for destruction. (13) Do not call out today for one destruction, but call out for many destructions﴾ [al-Furqan 13, 14]. It is also related in the lengthy, well-known hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib concerning the dying person and what happens after death that Allah, glorified and exalted, says: "Record the book of My servant in Sijjin" — meaning the disbeliever — "in the lowest, seventh earth"[[Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah (12059), Ahmad (18534), and al-Bayhaqi in Ithbat 'adhab al-qabr (44), from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, may Allah be pleased with him. The wording in al-Bayhaqi is: "Record his book in Sijjin, in the lowest seventh earth." In Ibn Abi Shaybah's wording: "Record the book of My servant in Sijjin, in the lowest earth."]]. So "Sijjin" is the lowest point of the earth, which is the dwelling place of the Fire — we seek refuge with Allah from it — and this record is in Sijjin.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, magnified this Sijjin by His saying: ﴿And what will make you know what Sijjin is?﴾ So the interrogative here is for magnification; that is: what is it that informed you about Sijjin?! Have you searched for it?! Have you asked about it until it was explained to you?!

Magnification may be for the greatness of a thing in elevation, and it may be for the greatness of a thing in lowness. This magnification in (Sijjin) is not for its loftiness and exaltation, but for its baseness and descent.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿A written record﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 9]. The word ﴿kitab﴾ here does not refer back to Sijjin; rather it refers to ﴿kitab﴾ in His saying: ﴿Nay, indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjin﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 7]. So what is this record?

He said: ﴿A written record﴾, meaning: a book that is inscribed, to which nothing is added and from which nothing is taken away, and which is not altered or changed. Rather, this is their final destination and their abode—and we seek refuge with Allah—for ever and ever.

"Book inscribed" (Qur'an 83:9) — the passage's verse quote begins with 9, but the translation below follows the text as given.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 83, verse 10–12:

﴿A book inscribed (9). Woe on that Day to the deniers﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 9, 10]. ﴾﴿Woe (waylun)﴾: The discussion of it has already passed in this surah, and we said that it is a word of threat, by which Allah threatens whoever deserves the threat, and it occurs often in the Noble Qur'an.

﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers (10). Those who deny the Day of Judgment﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 10, 11]. The whole discourse is about the Day of Judgment from the beginning of the surah to its end; it is all about the Day of Religion and recompense. Those who deny the Day of Judgment, Allah has threatened them with woe, because those who deny the Day of Judgment cannot possibly remain upright upon the Law of Allah. Only one who believes in the Day of Judgment remains upright upon the Law of Allah, for whoever does not believe in it, and believes only in this life, does not concern himself with what lies beyond it and does not work for it, and remains like the cattle: ﴿They enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat, and the Fire is their abode﴾ [Muhammad: 12].

For this reason, I think you know with me that Allah always joins faith in Him with faith in the Last Day, because faith in Allah is the beginning and faith in the Last Day is the end. You believe in Allah and then work for the Last Day, which is the final abode. These people—may Allah protect us—denied the Day of Judgment, and whoever denies it can never work for it, because action is built upon belief; if you have no belief, how can you work?! For this reason He said: ﴿None denies it except every transgressor sinful﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 12]. That is: none denies the Day of Judgment and rejects it ﴿except every transgressor sinful﴾, meaning: transgressing in his deeds and sinful in his words. It was also said: transgressing in his deeds and sinful in his earnings, i.e., his end is sin. The two meanings are close. The important point is that no one can deny the Day of Judgment except a man who is transgressing, sinful, one who earns sins that lead him to the Fire of Hell—we seek refuge in Allah.

For this reason, I think you know with me that Allah always joins faith in Him with faith in the Last Day, because faith in Allah is the beginning and faith in the Last Day is the end. You believe in Allah and then work for the Last Day, which is the final abode. These people—may Allah protect us—denied the Day of Judgment, and whoever denies it can never work for it, because action is built upon belief; if you have no belief, how can you work?! For this reason He said: ﴿None denies it except every transgressor sinful﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 12]. That is: none denies the Day of Judgment and rejects it ﴿except every transgressor sinful﴾, meaning: transgressing in his deeds and sinful in his words. It was also said: transgressing in his deeds and sinful in his earnings, i.e., his end is sin. The two meanings are close. The important point is that no one can deny the Day of Judgment except a man who is transgressing, sinful, one who earns sins that lead him to the Fire of Hell—we seek refuge in Allah.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 83, verse 13:

﴿When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Tales of the ancients!"﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 13]. ﴿When Our verses are recited to him﴾ means: when anyone recites them to him. This indicates that this man does not think of reciting the verses of Allah himself, but they are recited to him; so when they are recited to him he says, "Tales of the ancients!" That is, "These are the tales of the ancients."

﴿Asatir﴾ is the plural of ustura (a fable, a myth), which is speech that is mentioned for amusement, having no reality or basis. So he says, "This Qur'an is the tales of the ancients." Why does he not benefit from the Qur'an, when it is the most eloquent of speech and the most powerful in its effect on the heart, to the point that Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart or gives ear while he is a witness﴾ [Qaf: 37]?

(...) That none denies the Day of Judgment except every transgressor, sinful, the verse clarifies the condition of this man: when he is called to the truth and to affirming the report of Allah, he does not accept that. ﴿When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Tales of the ancients!"﴾ meaning that these are fables and idle tales, only for occupying gatherings and entertaining oneself with them. That is because he, may Allah protect us, was not a believer, so the light of the verses of Allah the Mighty and Majestic does not reach his heart, and he sees them as like the tales of the ancients which old women and elders speak, having no reality and no seriousness whatsoever.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Nay!﴾ That is, "They are not the fables of the ancients." Rather, ﴿these people, [their hearts are covered with what they used to earn]﴾: that is, it has gathered upon their hearts and veiled them from the truth.

﴿Nay! Rather, upon their hearts is [the] rust of what they used to earn﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 14]. That is, of evil deeds, because evil deeds come between a person and guidance, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [Muhammad 17]. Whoever is guided by the guidance of Allah, follows what Allah has commanded, abandons what Allah has forbidden, believes in what Allah has informed of, and does the like in what has come from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then there is no doubt that his heart is illuminated, that he sees the truth as truth and falsehood as falsehood, and that he magnifies the signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and sees that they are above every speech, and that the guidance of Muhammad (ﷺ) is above every guidance. This is the one whose heart Allah has illuminated with faith.

As for one whose heart has been stained, may Allah protect us, with the filth and impurities of sins, he does not see these signs as true; rather, he sees them only as the fables of the ancients, as in this verse.

﴿Nay! Rather, upon their hearts is [the] rust of what they used to earn﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 14]. There is a subtle pause at ﴿بَلْ﴾ according to some reciters, while others make no pause there. It is therefore permissible to say ﴿كَلَّا بَل رَّانَ﴾, and it is permissible to say ﴿كَلَّا بَلْ رَانَ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ مَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾. This does not change the meaning; whether you pause or do not pause, the meaning does not change.

﴿Nay, indeed they will be veiled from their Lord that Day﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 15]. That is, truly, they will be veiled from their Lord. This occurs on the Day of Resurrection, for they will be prevented from seeing Allah, Mighty and Majestic, just as they were veiled from seeing His law and His signs, so they regarded them as "the fables of the ancients."

By this verse, Ahl al-Sunna wa al-Jama'ah (the People of the Sunnah and the Community) have argued for the affirmation of the vision of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The basis of the argument is clear: the fact that these people are veiled in a state of displeasure implies that the righteous are granted the vision of Him, Exalted, in a state of contentment. If these are the veiled, then the righteous are not veiled. And if the veiling applied to all of them, there would be no benefit at all in specifying it for the wicked.

The vision of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is established by the Book, by the mutawatir (mass-transmitted) Sunnah, and by the consensus (ijma') of the Companions and the imams. There is no doubt that He, Exalted, will truly be seen with the eye, as He said: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 22-23]. He, Exalted, also said: ﴿For those who did good is the best reward and more﴾ [Yunus: 26]. The Prophet (ﷺ) explained "more" as looking at the Face of Allah, Exalted. Similarly, He said: ﴿For them is whatever they wish therein, and with Us is more﴾ [Qaf: 35], where "more" (mazid) has the same meaning as "more" (ziyadah) in His words: ﴿For those who did good is the best reward and more﴾. And He said: ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision﴾ [al-An'am: 103]. The negation of grasping (idrak) indicates the affirmation of the basic fact of seeing (ru'yah). For this reason, this verse was cited by the salaf (early generations) as evidence for the vision of Allah, while some of the khalaf (later generations) cited it as evidence against the vision of Allah. Undoubtedly, the verse is evidence against them, because Allah did not negate seeing by it; He negated only grasping, and the negation of grasping indicates the affirmation of the basic fact of seeing. The conclusion is that the Qur'an indicates the truth of the vision of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with the eye.

Likewise, the Sunnah has come explicitly to this effect, where the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Indeed, you will see your Lord plainly, just as you see the sun when there are no clouds over it"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (7435) from the hadith of Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah (may Allah be pleased with him).]], and: "Indeed, you will see your Lord just as you see the moon on the night of the full moon, and you will not be harmed in seeing Him"[[Narrated with this wording by al-Tirmidhi (2554) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him). The hadith is agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh): al-Bukhari (554) and Muslim (633/211), from the hadith of Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah (may Allah be pleased with him) with a similar wording.]]. The Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) and those who followed them in excellence among the early generations of this Ummah and its imams believed in this. Those whose minds and hearts were veiled from the truth denied it, saying: "Allah cannot possibly be seen with the eye," and that the intended meaning of "seeing" in the verses is the seeing of the heart, i.e., certainty (yaqin). There is no doubt that this is a false view, contrary to the Qur'an, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the salaf. Moreover, certainty is attainable by others as well; even the wicked on the Day of Resurrection will see what they were promised as truth and will be certain of it. This is not the place to elaborate on establishing the vision of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, or to debate the evidences of the two sides, because the matter, praise be to Allah, is clearer than that it should require lengthy discussion.

﴿Nay, indeed they, that Day, will be veiled from their Lord. Then indeed they will surely burn in the Blazing Fire.﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 15, 16]

Indeed, these wicked ones will surely burn in Hellfire; i.e., they will enter it, experiencing its heat and its punishment. We ask Allah for well-being.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 83, verse 17:

﴿Then it will be said﴾ as a rebuke and reproach to them, ﴿"This is what you used to deny."﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 17]. So the punishment of the body and the pain of the body are combined in them through being burned in the Fire, and likewise the punishment of the heart through reproach and remorse, when it is said: "This is what you used to deny." For this reason they will say: ﴿"Would that we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers."﴾ [al-An'am 27]. God Most High said: ﴿"Rather, there has appeared to them what they had been concealing before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars."﴾ [al-An'am 28].

* * *
﴿

﴾﴿﴾We have discussed the tafsir (exegesis) that we began from Surah al-Nabaʾ until we reached the saying of Allah, the Exalted:

﴿Nay, indeed the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyin﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 18], from Surah al-Mutaffifin. In this verse, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentions a statement emphasized by (إنَّ) (inna), because (إنَّ) in the Arabic language is one of the particles of emphasis. When you say (الرجلُ قائمٌ) (al-rajulu qaʾimun, "the man is standing"), this is an unemphasized statement. When you say (إنَّ الرجلَ قائمٌ) (inna al-rajula qaʾimun, "indeed the man is standing"), it becomes an emphasized statement.

So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Indeed, the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyin﴾. This is the counterpart of ﴿Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin﴾. The record of the wicked is in Sijjin, at the bottom of the earth, and the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyin, at the highest part of Paradise; that is, they are in this lofty place. It was decreed with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth.

﴿And what will make you know what ʿIlliyyūn is?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 19] That is: what is it that informed you of what ʿIlliyyūn is?! This interrogative is intended to express magnification and exaltation. The meaning is: by what could you know it?! For it is great.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿A written record﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 20]. This is an explanation of His words: ﴿Indeed, the record of the righteous﴾; meaning, indeed the record of the righteous is a written record, inscribed, which does not change or alter.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 83, verse 21:

﴿Witnessed by those brought near (to Allah).﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin: 21] That is: it is attended (by them), or those brought near witness to it. The "muqarrabun" (those brought near) with Allah are those who drew near to Allah, may He be exalted, through obedience to Him. The more a person is obedient to Allah, the closer he is to Allah; and the more a person is humble before Allah, the more honoured and the higher he is in the sight of Allah. Allah, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Allah will raise those among you who believe and those who have been given knowledge, by degrees﴾ [Al-Mujadilah: 11]. So the muqarrabun are those who drew near to Allah, may He be exalted, through righteous deeds, and so Allah brought them near to Himself.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 83, verse 22:

﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss. Upon couches, they will look on.﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 22, 23] ﴿Al-abrar﴾ is the plural of barr (pious, righteous). Al-barr is one who has abundant good, abundant obedience, and abundant beneficence, both in worshipping Allah and in dealing kindly with the servants of Allah. Thus, these righteous ones, upon whom Allah has bestowed the doing of good deeds and the abandoning of evil deeds, will be in bliss.

﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss.﴾ Here, "bliss" (na'im) encompasses the bliss of the body and the bliss of the heart. As for the bliss of the body, do not ask about it. Allah, glorified and exalted, said about Paradise: ﴿Therein is what the souls desire and what the eyes delight in, and you will abide therein eternally﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 71]. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for their eyes as a reward for what they used to do﴾ [as-Sajdah: 17]. As for the bliss of the heart, do not ask about that either. It will be said to them, when they have seen death slaughtered: "O people of Paradise, eternity without death!"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4730), Muslim (2849/40), and an-Nasa'i (168), with his wording, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him).]] It will be said to them: ﴿Enter it in peace﴾ [al-Hijr: 46; Qaf: 34]. It will be said to them: "Indeed, for you is that you will have bliss and never be miserable, that you will be healthy and never be sick, and that you will be youthful and never grow old."[[Muslim (2837/22) narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with them both), from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "A caller will call out: Indeed, for you is that you will be healthy and never fall ill, that you will live and never die, that you will be youthful and never grow old, and that you will have bliss and never be miserable. This is His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿And they will be called: This is the Paradise you have been made to inherit for what you used to do﴾ [al-A'raf: 43]."]] All of this brings joy to the heart, so they attain both the bliss of the heart and the bliss of the body. The angels enter upon them from every gate, saying to them: ﴿Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured; how excellent is the final abode﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 24]. May Allah make me and you among them.

And the Most High's saying: ﴿Upon couches, they will gaze﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 23]. "Al-ara'ik" is the plural of "arika" (canopied couch), which is a decorated, adorned couch on which a canopy-like covering is placed, and it is among the most splendid kinds of beds. So they are ﴿upon couches﴾, upon these soft, goodly, beautiful beds, ﴿gazing﴾, meaning: gazing upon what Allah has bestowed upon them of bliss that souls cannot now comprehend; ﴿no soul knows what is kept hidden for them of the delight of the eyes﴾.

Some scholars said: this gazing includes even the gazing upon the Face of Allah, and they made this verse one of the proofs for the affirmation of the seeing of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in Paradise.

You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss (تعرف في وجوههم نضرة النعيم). That is: O observer, you will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss, meaning its goodliness and splendor, i.e., the enjoyment of luxury (التنعُّم). And you witness now in this world that the pampered and affluent, their faces are not like the faces of the toilers who labor. You find them radiant, you find them goodly, you find them pampered. So the people of Paradise, the radiance of bliss is recognized in their faces, i.e., the enjoyment of luxury (التنعُّم) and joy, because they are at their most joyful and at their most blessed.

Then Allah, may He be exalted, said, describing their bliss: ﴿They will be given to drink of a sealed pure wine﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 25], and so on to its end.

We will discuss it, God willing, in the next session.

* * *

(...) We continue with Surah al-Mutaffifin, where we stopped at the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿They will be given to drink of a sealed pure wine, its seal is musk; and for that let the competitors compete﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 25–26].

The pronoun in His saying ﴿They will be given to drink﴾ refers to the righteous (al-abrar). Allah, mighty and majestic, gives them to drink through the hands of the servants whom Allah described in His saying: ﴿There will circulate among them young boys made eternal, with cups and jugs and a cup from a flowing spring. They will not be affected by headache from it, nor will they be intoxicated﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 17–19].

﴿They will be given to drink of a sealed pure wine﴾ means: a drink that is pure, unmixed with anything, harmless to the mind, and not causing any pain in the head, unlike the drink of this world, which takes away the mind and causes headache. That one is pure wine (rahiq) with no harm whatsoever.

﴿Sealed (makhtum) [25]. Its seal is musk﴾ means: its last part and its end is musk; that is, it is fragrant. This is unlike the wine of this world, which has a foul smell. These righteous people, since they restrained themselves from the pleasures that Allah forbade them in this world, will be given them on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And for that let the competitors compete﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 26] means: in this reward and recompense, ﴿let the competitors compete﴾, that is, let those who race race with a race that brings them to the limit of breath, which is a metaphor for speed in competing. It is said: "I competed with him (nafastuhu)," meaning, I raced him a race that brought me to exhaustion of breath.

Competition in goodness (al-munafasah fi al-khayr) is racing toward the obedience of Allah, mighty and majestic, and toward what pleases Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and keeping far from what angers Allah.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim (27), a spring from which those brought near drink﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 27, 28]. That is: the mixture of this drink which is given to these righteous ones is ﴿from Tasnim﴾, meaning from a spring that is elevated in meaning and in sensory reality. This is because the rivers of Paradise gush forth from al-Firdaws, and al-Firdaws is the highest part of Paradise and its middle part, and above it is the Throne of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, as has been established from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So this drink is mixed with this fragrance that comes from Tasnim; that is, from the elevated, lofty, high place, which is the Garden of Eden.

﴿a spring from which those brought near drink﴾: that is, this spring, and the gushing waters and flowing rivers, from which those brought near drink.

Here someone will say: why did He say ﴿drink from it﴾ (yashrabu biha)? Is it a vessel that is carried, so that one would say "he drank with the vessel"?

The answer: No, because a spring or a river is not carried.

So why did He not say "those brought near drink from it" (yashrabu minha)?

The answer to this difficulty is one of two views. Some scholars said: the particle "ba" (bi) here has the meaning of "min" (from), so the meaning of ﴿yashrabu biha﴾ is "drink from it".

Others said: the verb ﴿yashrabu﴾ (drink) is used with the implied meaning of "yarwa" (to be quenched/satisfied), so the meaning of ﴿yashrabu biha﴾ is "those brought near are quenched by it". This second view is better than the previous one, because it includes two things, which strengthen it:

First: keeping the preposition on its original meaning.

Second: the verb ﴿yashrabu﴾ has been given a meaning higher than mere drinking, which is quenching (al-riyy). For many a person drinks without being quenched, but once one is quenched, one has indeed drunk.

Accordingly, the second view is better, namely that the verb ﴿yashrabu﴾ is understood to mean "yarwa" (is quenched).

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 83, verse 29:

﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed.﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 29].

﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes﴾ i.e., those who engaged in crime (jurm), which is disobedience and opposition, ﴿used to﴾ i.e., in the worldly life, ﴿laugh at those who believed﴾ mocking them, deriding them, and belittling them.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 83, verse 30:

﴿And when they passed by them, they winked at one another.﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 30]. In ﴿when they passed by﴾, who is the subject: is it those who committed sin, or those who believed?

The verse is suitable for both. It is possible that it means: when the believers passed by the criminals, or: when the criminals passed by the believers. The principle you should understand in tafsir (exegesis of the Qur'an) is that if a verse can carry two meanings that do not contradict each other, it must be understood as having both meanings, because that is more comprehensive. Is this clear to you? ﴿And when they passed by them, they winked at one another.﴾ Who is the one passing by? This is a question directed at you.

* Students: (...).

* The Shaykh: It may mean: when the criminals passed by the believers, or: when the believers passed by the criminals. If we take it as referring to both, the meaning becomes that when the criminals passed by the believers while the believers were sitting, the criminals winked at one another, and when the believers passed by the criminals while the criminals were sitting, they also winked at one another. So the verse includes both situations: the situation of criminals passing by believers, and the situation of believers passing by criminals.

﴿they winked at one another﴾ means: some of them nudge others, saying: "Look at these people," in mockery, derision and belittling.

﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting.﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin: 31]

"When the criminals returned to their families" ﴿they returned jesting﴾, meaning: amusing themselves with the mockery they had directed at these believers. They ridicule, scoff, and take delight in this, thinking that they had succeeded and had overcome the believers. But the matter is the opposite.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when they see them, they say, "Indeed, these are [astray]."﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 32].

﴿And when they see them﴾, i.e., when the criminals see the believers, ﴿they say, "Indeed, these are [astray]."﴾ Astray from the correct path, backward, rigid, extremist... and other such labels.

These people of the past have had successors in our time, and before and after it. Among people there are those who say of the people of goodness: "They are reactionaries, they are backward." And they call the one who is committed (to religion): "He is extremist and rigid." And above all this, there are those who said of the Messengers: "They are sorcerers or madmen." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Thus did there come no messenger to those before them except that they said, "A sorcerer or a madman!"﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat 52]. So the heirs of the Messengers, from among the people of knowledge and religion, will be struck by what the enemies of the Messengers inflicted upon the Messengers of insulting labels, mockery, and the like. Among this is the labeling by the people of innovation, the people of ta'til (negation of divine attributes), of the Salaf, the people of ithbat (affirmation of divine attributes), as "hashawiyya" (literalist fillers), "mujassima" (anthropomorphists), "mushabbiha" (likeners), and other such insulting labels by which they repel people from the straight path.

﴿When they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are surely astray." (32) But they had not been sent to watch over them.﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 32-33]

That is, these criminals were not sent as guardians over these people, to observe them and pass judgment on them. Rather, judgment belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Then Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 34]. ﴿Today﴾ means: on the Day of Resurrection, those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers. So ﴿those who believed﴾ (alladhina) is the subject (mubtada'), and ﴿will laugh﴾ (yadhakun) is its predicate (khabar), and ﴿at the disbelievers﴾ (min al-kuffar) is connected to ﴿will laugh﴾. The meaning: so those who believed will laugh today at the disbelievers. By Allah, this is the laughter after which there is no weeping. As for the mockery of the criminals toward the believers in this world, it will be followed by weeping, sorrow, woe and perdition.

On the couches they will gaze.

That is, indeed the believers are on couches in Paradise, and the arā'ik (couches) are the splendid, fine, luxurious beds.

"On the couches they will gaze": that is, they will look upon what Allah has prepared for them of reward, and they will look upon those who used to mock them in the world, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿A speaker among them will say, "Indeed, I had a companion who used to say, 'Are you really among those who believe? When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be recompensed?'" He will say, "Would you like to look down?" [As-Saffat 51–54]. He says to his companions in Paradise, offering them the chance to look down upon his companion who in the world denied and rejected the Resurrection. ﴿So he looked down and saw him in the midst of the Blazing Fire﴾ [As-Saffat 55], at its depths and its base. He said to him, ﴿"By Allah, you almost brought me to ruin! And had it not been for the favor of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forth [to the Fire]"﴾ [As-Saffat 56–57]. So you now see that the believers see the disbelievers as they are being punished in the depths of the Fire, while the believers are in Paradise.

He said: ﴿On the couches they will gaze.﴾ So they will look upon two things:

The first thing: what Allah has prepared for them of bliss, including gazing upon the Face of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The second: they will look upon those disbelievers who, in the world, used to mock them and ridicule them, looking at them while they are in the punishment of Allah.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Have the disbelievers been recompensed for what they used to do?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 36].

﴿Thuwwiba﴾ means: was repaid, or requited. The particle ﴿hal﴾ here is for confirmation (taqrir); that is, Allah, the Exalted, has indeed recompensed the disbelievers and requited them with the due reward of their deeds in this world. He, glorified and exalted, is the Just Judge, so His judgment revolves between justice and bounty. With regard to those who believed, His judgment and recompense is bounty (fadl); with regard to the disbelievers, His judgment and recompense is justice ('adl). So all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

With this, the commentary on Surah al-Mutaffifin, which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made easy, is complete. We ask Allah, the Exalted, to benefit us and you by it, and to make us among those who take heed and admonish others.
